html:
In February 1568 the Spanish navigator Álvaro de Mendaña reached Santa Isabel, the first European to visit the islands he named the Islas de Salomón, hoping they held King Solomon's gold.

He had sailed from Peru looking for a southern continent. His men fought with islanders over food, and he found no gold. Mendaña returned in 1595 to found a colony on Santa Cruz, but he died there and the settlers left.

Europeans then lost track of the islands for almost two centuries. When ships returned in the late 1700s, the old Spanish name was kept. Traders and labour recruiters followed; see blackbirding and the British protectorate. Compare Magellan.
